e648cb3f4436.en: Version 0.15.0 brings the companion app to Omarchy and makes the deck a dictation microphone there. The deck's firmware is unchanged at 0.14.0.

ea82dcc2e1a6.en: The app the Mac and Windows have now runs on Omarchy (Hyprland), as OpenWalkieTalkie in the app launcher, with the same five pages: Deck, Faces & Keys, Integrations, Voice and Service. It finds the service by itself. Service starts and stops the service through its systemd user unit, and Open at login is an XDG autostart entry. There is no tray icon, which is the desktop bar's job, and no in-app update, because the app is built from source.

29f372bbcb72.en: Faces & Keys also fits a tiled window narrower than the app's design: the face strip wraps onto a second row and the key editor goes under the key grid. The Omarchy guide covers building and installing it.

a82083a092d2.en: On the Omarchy face, PTT works like Superwhisper's own push-to-talk. Hold it and talk, release, and your words are typed at the cursor of whatever window has the keyboard, with no Enter. CANCEL while you hold throws the recording away. Superwhisper does the recognition when it is installed, in its own mode, language and vocabulary; otherwise the local Whisper model does. The bridge puts a Dictate entry on the roster for this, and selecting it on the Agents face dictates the same way.

bc936f2cdd87.en: On the Omarchy face the wheel now moves through the window rows in the order the face lists them, the way it moves through the deck's other lists, and stops at the first and last row. It used to follow Hyprland's own window order, so a turn could skip the row below.

9bf7e8496843.en: The Linux service now keeps everything in one folder, ~/.local/share/openwalkietalkie, as one folder holds it on a Mac. Omarchy installs already ran there, and deckd commands no longer need the DECKD_DATA_DIR=… prefix. If you ran deckd by hand on Linux with the earlier layout, move its files to that folder or set DECKD_DATA_DIR.

a0e318bb31b3.en: On a Mac, choose Check for Updates…, or install the signed, notarized 0.15.0 app for Apple Silicon or Intel (macOS 13 or later). On Windows, download the ZIP from the release. 7ab5bd2d67bb.en: The storage percentage means free space. It changes color as space runs low. Missing counters show Not available, readings older than ten seconds turn gray and show STALE, and a lost host shows OFFLINE. The first CPU percentage needs two samples.

4a44d64de337.en: Readings arrive every two seconds, but unchanged meters do not redraw. This is a deck-only page; subscription allowances stay on Usage, and there is no extra Mac app page.

174cf69b3cff.en: A 360-frame renderer test with multiple and recycled pipes transfers 51.5% fewer pixels on average. That is a transfer-area measurement, not an on-device frame-rate claim. Partial frames are checked against full redraws through score changes, pause and game over. TE synchronization remains disabled, so this is not a promise of tear-free animation.

fcfeb68f7bac.en: Music that has room to develop

40f26aa55905.en: When you talk to a Conol chat from the deck, the words should be the ones Conol would have heard if you had typed into it. Version 0.12.0 hands those presses to Conol's own speech model, shows you a recording timeline while you talk, mirrors what Conol is doing right now, and adds a Timer face with Pomodoro.

195e6be11203.en: Hold PTT on a Conol chat or + New chat and the Mac service records the press and passes it to the Conol desktop app. Conol transcribes it with the cloud speech model behind its composer's microphone, and that text is what the deck shows after release and what is sent, including dictated answers to Conol's questions.

160ee60274db.en: The Mac's own recognizer keeps running during the press. If Conol can't answer, fails, or takes longer than 20 seconds, the Mac's transcript is used, so a press is never lost. Other agents and naming the deck stay on your Mac. Only presses addressed to Conol chats leave the Mac, and only to the Conol app you are signed in to; set [voice.stt] companion = false to keep every press local. This needs the updated Conol desktop and web versions; with an older Conol app, nothing changes.

6a1126568043.en: The Mac's live words are not what Conol will hear, so the deck no longer shows them for these presses. Instead it shows RECORDING, a large elapsed time and a timeline: a red playhead walks left to right while the waveform of your voice, measured by the deck's own microphone, fills in behind it. Long presses scroll. After release the deck shows TRANSCRIBING, then Conol's transcript.

08ce492d4622.en: A running Conol chat now shows its current public step on the deck, such as "Running a command" with a short preview, both in the roster and in the conversation. It updates in place and clears when the step ends. Full tool inputs and results stay in Conol.

06a7f08c1266.en: Add Timer from the face manager's + gallery for a stopwatch with laps, a countdown with presets, and Pomodoro: 25 minutes of focus and 5-minute breaks, with a 15-minute break after four focus sessions. Each phase waits for Next / Enter. The timers run on the deck itself, keep going on other pages and while the screen sleeps, and wake the screen with a toast when they finish.

1d34eb2e640c.en: Any native companion with its own recognizer can register caps.transcribe: "push", receive agent.transcribe offers, page the 16 kHz WAV with agent.transcribe.audio and answer with agent.transcribe.result. c13f4f4a6adc.en: Desktop tasks reach the shared service

31fdda593aa0.en: The previous launcher could open Desktop successfully while leaving its conversations invisible to OpenWalkieTalkie. Desktop’s default plugin settings caused its implicit shared-service mode to fall back to a private server. The updated launcher selects the shared local connection explicitly.

d0bf350961cf.en: Compatible installations named either ChatGPT.app or Codex.app are detected. The launcher reuses the existing Codex service and leaves running Desktop tasks alone. A separate fix restores replies from short tasks that finish before OpenWalkieTalkie subscribes to their conversation.

ce302e7584d5.en: Install the 0.5.0 app and check that its service also reports 0.5.0. Open Integrations → Codex Desktop and install or repair the integration. When your Desktop tasks are idle, quit Codex Desktop / ChatGPT and open ~/Applications/Codex with OpenWalkieTalkie.app.

d06c719ef23f.en: This is a small launcher for your installed Desktop app. Use it for future launches too: opening the original app directly does not enable the shared connection. Unsupported Desktop builds produce an error instead of silently opening a disconnected session.

765bbd2b6982.en: More flash options and factory images

f37d9c60278b.en: The firmware now accepts Puya PY25Q128HA-SUH-IR (C5354566) and GigaDevice GD25Q128ESIGR (C2928891), alongside the existing Winbond W25Q128JVSIQ (C97521). Its settings, pairing, and bootloader writers verify a stable supported chip ID before enabling writes. Boards populated with the alternative parts still need physical qualification.

c562cd786385.en: The release includes a factory ZIP with separate 16 MiB images for Rev A and Rev B. Each combines the exact released application and recovery binaries with a fresh flash table and empty unit storage. Chinese instructions, component hashes, and a standalone verifier are included.

5e564b0477dd.en: Factory images overwrite all flash contents, including settings and pairing data. They are for blank-board provisioning. Existing devices should use the app’s normal USB updater.

5aa9d6cb93d8.en: Connect one deck over USB-C and open Service → Updates → Check firmware. The partition layout and recovery protocol are unchanged from 0.4.0, so devices already on recovery protocol 2 receive a normal application update.

323d43db6bf9.en: Devices still on the old bootloader need the guided migration. Do not manually install bootstrap or recovery files as application firmware.

e4f0fdd17e92.en: The launcher and transport regression tests pass. In a live test on the development Mac, Desktop connected to the shared service and its DESKTOP-LINK-OK reply appeared in the OpenWalkieTalkie GUI. USB delivery to the connected Rev A was healthy; the final physical screen check was not recorded.

421881316c03.en: Both board variants pass software checks. The preceding 0.4.1 development firmware with the same flash support completed an old-bootloader migration on the existing Rev A. The CI-built 0.5.0 files were not flashed in that test. A shipped Rev B, boards with the alternate chips, and blank-board factory programming still need hardware validation. 4ab32ec178b1.en: Two minutes to lock, four ticks to unlock

3b22cb017bec.en: After two minutes without local input, the display sleeps and every local control locks, including push-to-talk. Pressing a button, touching the screen, or turning the wheel lights the lock screen without activating the control underneath.

90fa8176f47e.en: To unlock, turn the wheel counterclockwise four consecutive ticks. If the first tick wakes the display, it counts toward the four. Turning clockwise or letting the display sleep again resets your progress.

6e5eb72f6c30.en: The final unlocking tick only unlocks the deck; it does not also move the selection. A button held while locked must be released and pressed again before it can act, so a trapped PTT cannot start transmitting as the deck unlocks. 06a787763988.en: EQ before audio reaches the speaker

68cc12839701.en: The service processes mixed speech and chimes before sending them over USB or Bluetooth LE. The preset combines a 250 Hz high-pass filter with cuts of 5 dB at 1.1 kHz and 6 dB at 6.3 kHz. It leaves 3 dB of headroom and limits samples to −1 dBFS.

9ccc09b23939.en: Filter state carries across audio blocks and silence, then resets when the output reopens. Invalid samples cannot spoil subsequent audio.

dab737384b9c.en: The preset is enabled automatically for the custom 16 kHz device audio output; there is no EQ toggle in this release. It does not boost the speaker's deep bass or narrow response dips, so bass-heavy material can sound quieter. Locally generated Arcade audio, legacy CoreAudio output, and raw measurement tones are unchanged.

7aada430795d.en: Less flash activity on Rev A

5441dcb7d39f.en: Rev A's code, constants, and font assets are copied into PSRAM at startup, with interrupt vectors in SRAM. Startup verifies the copies and returns to USB recovery after three failed attempts. Rev B and LilyGo continue to execute from NOR flash.

The service checks that capability automatically, keeps EQ enabled, and falls back to 16 kHz for older firmware. 698c260f1cba.en: This improves the playback path; it does not create detail that was absent from the source voice. Our Kokoro test voice produced 24 kHz audio. Sending it through the 48 kHz path avoids the earlier reduction to 16 kHz and changes the compression and reconstruction path as well.

82e82eb7725b.en: The host now searches alternative ADPCM encoding paths to reduce quantization error, keeping the original result whenever it is better. The firmware replaces linear interpolation with a band-limited filter before sending 16 kHz audio to the 48 kHz DAC.

d920433ce1d5.en: On the same English passage, the revised encoder reduced squared encoding error by about 30%. That is a digital measurement, not a promise of complete audible hiss removal: the revised 16 kHz path still needs that listening confirmation.

e17ccc0b752a.en: BLE playback and microphone capture remain at 16 kHz. The USB comparison completed without gaps, underruns, queue drops, or sequence errors at either rate. Sustained 48 kHz playback over BLE has not been validated, so this release keeps the higher rate specific to USB.

dc676ad5d9ed.en: The socket is the one door for connected apps. The service's HTTP and WebSocket door on 127.0.0.1, and the bearer tokens that open it, are off by default. 3c09fe6a166b.en: app_id is a stable application identifier (1–64 ASCII letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores). group_id identifies an account or workspace within the app (1–128 UTF-8 bytes). group_label is its visible heading (1–24 UTF-8 bytes). 0920268ff3b3.en: FOLLOW ONE TASK FROM START TO FINISH

03a419287002.en: Complete one agent setup first. Keep its conversation open on your Mac so you can see exactly where your deck sends the message. The screen images below are examples, not your live sessions.

96178d25b7fe.en: ON THE DECK: Press CANCEL to return from a conversation to Agents. LEFT / RIGHT changes project pages; SCROLL moves the highlight. Select your project and agent, then press ENTER to open it.

2aaaae2145d6.en: CHECK → The conversation title matches the one open on your Mac. Touch alternative: tap a row to select, then tap it again to open.

02f3c12809db.en: ON THE DECK: Hold the left-side PTT button. Check the agent name and LISTENING indicator. Say: “Summarize this project and tell me what to do next.” Release PTT to send. To discard the recording, press CANCEL while still in the PTT session.

3dac550991e1.en: ON THE MAC → Your spoken request reaches that session. Use Voice → Test Voice to check recognition beforehand; a listening screen alone does not prove delivery.

79beac12a7df.en: ON THE DECK: Wait for the agent to work and return a reply. SCROLL browses the conversation. Hold SHIFT and press ENTER to return to the latest messages. LEFT / RIGHT switches to the previous / next agent; CANCEL returns to the roster.

2f581ef61443.en: ON THE MAC → The assistant works in its normal project conversation. The deck shows the linked history and status; it does not run the coding assistant by itself.

90aad4a9ec56.en: ON THE DECK: Tap the question notice, or press ENTER on a conversation with a pending card. Read the question, turn SCROLL to choose, then press ENTER to submit. CANCEL snoozes the card; it does not choose “No”. Swipe down from the top to find it again.

a0e8187a9e8f.en: ON THE MAC → The answer resolves the corresponding question. If “not delivered” appears, check the session and answer there. Read the actual options before confirming; the pictured question is only an example.

099a7792bce1.en: Hold PTT again on the same conversation and ask a follow-up. In Codex, the message starts a turn when idle or steers a running turn. In Claude Code, it reaches the connected session through Channels or its fallback inbox. The companion window does not display conversation text.

16d617b7d850.en: Turn to move the highlight; in a conversation, turn to read older messages. Hold SHIFT + press ENTER to follow the latest reply again.

cdcc00581f5f.en: Hold to record for the selected agent; release to send. Press CANCEL during recording to discard. In Arcade, PTT controls the game.

94112ec57a47.en: Hold SHIFT and turn SCROLL to change face. Release SHIFT before selecting a row. Double-tap SHIFT to open the face manager.

879c82188708.en: Hold SHIFT + turn to Arcade. SCROLL chooses a game and ENTER opens it. Use the game controls on page 8; CANCEL returns to the list. PTT does not record here.
